import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 489

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/489](https://www.erdosproblems.com/489)
-/

namespace Erdos489

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The set of positive integers not divisible by any element of `A`. -/
def sievedSet (A : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ := {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, ¬(a ∣ n)}

/-- The squared-gap sum `∑_{b_i < x} (b_{i+1} - b_i)²`, where `b_i` enumerates the positive
integers not divisible by any element of `A`. -/
noncomputable def GapSumSq (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  letI B := sievedSet A
  let b := Nat.nth (· ∈ B)
  ∑ i < Nat.count (· ∈ B) x, ((b (i + 1) : ℝ) - b i) ^ 2

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set such that $\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert=o(x^{1/2})$. Let
$B=\{ n\geq 1 : a\nmid n\textrm{ for all }a\in A\}$.
If $B=\{b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ then is it true that
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{b_i < x}(b_{i+1}-b_i)^2$$
exists (and is finite)?

For example, when $A=\{p^2: p\textrm{ prime}\}$ then $B$ is the set of squarefree numbers,
and the existence of this limit was proved by Erdős.

See also [208].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-489/F061/Erdos489.lean"]
theorem erdos_489 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
      (fun x : ℕ => (((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter (· ∈ A)).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
        (fun x : ℕ => (x : ℝ).sqrt) →
      (sievedSet A).Infinite →
      ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => GapSumSq A x / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  sorry

/-- When $A = \{p^2 : p \textrm{ prime}\}$, $B$ is the set of squarefree numbers, and the
existence of this limit was proved by Erdős. This is the $\alpha = 2$ case of Erdős Problem 145. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_489.variants.squarefree :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto
      (fun x : ℕ => GapSumSq {n | ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n = p ^ 2} x / (x : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  sorry

end Erdos489

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly assumes `(sievedSet A).Infinite`, whereas the source presupposes an infinite enumeration by writing B = {b₁ < b₂ < ⋯}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This makes the source's enumeration assumption explicit. Moreover, even if finite sieved sets are admitted using the total GapSumSq definition, their counting functions, and hence their gap-sum numerators, are eventually constant. Their normalized sums therefore tend to zero. In structural.lean I proved this finite-case limit and a general ↔ showing that imposing the infinitude restriction does not change the universal limit-existence assertion, for any additional hypothesis on A.

reformulations.difference: Both the sparsity hypothesis and the limit use natural-number cutoffs rather than real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For integer b, b < x iff b < ceil(x), so the real strict-cutoff sum is exactly the natural-cutoff sum evaluated at ceil(x). Since ceil(x)/x tends to 1, convergence of the normalized natural sums is equivalent to convergence over real cutoffs. The real counting function of A is the natural counting function evaluated at floor(x); its little-o relation to sqrt(x) is equivalent to the natural one by composition, sqrt(floor(x)) ≤ sqrt(x), and restriction back to integer inputs. Both generic equivalences were proved in real-parameter.lean.

reformulations.difference: Relative to the α = 2 formulation of Problem 145, this variant uses the strict cutoff bᵢ < x rather than bᵢ ≤ x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: At integer cutoffs, the non-strict sum at n equals the strict sum at n+1. Shifting the argument by one and replacing the normalization n+1 by n preserve existence and value of a finite limit. The generic convergence ↔ for F(n)/n and F(n+1)/n was proved in real-parameter.lean. I also proved that sieving by prime squares gives exactly Mathlib's squarefree naturals. Thus this is the stated squarefree special case, not a different gap statistic.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Boundary tests cover x = 0 and 1, insertion of 0 into A, 1 ∈ A, and satisfiable hypotheses with A empty. Kernel-checked squarefree examples give GapSumSq values 6, 17, and 18 at cutoffs 4, 10, and 11. The external proof targets Lean 4.31.0; adaptations for the installed 4.33.1 were three uses of a renamed Finset lemma, one instance-elaboration proof step, and a namespace closure needed when concatenating modules. No theorem statements were changed. In /workspace/review/external-proof-bridge.lean, `Review489.checked_main` proves exactly the committed main statement without invoking its sorry-backed theorem; its axioms are [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
